Volos New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nea Ionia, Greece

Not demolished. A small Romaniot community existed in Volos from the 14th century; 35 Peloponnesian families resettled there in the early 19th century, formally organizing the community. A Jewish school opened via the Alliance Israelite Universelle in 1864, followed by a new synagogue in 1865; population reached 190 by 1869, and the community became known for hospitality to travelers passing through Volos's port. A second Alliance school (1888-1926) preceded Rabbi Moshe Pesach's 1892 appointment, held until his death in 1955. Population reached about 500 by 1896, with Zionist activity from 1908 and further organizations through the 1920s; by 1939, 14 charity associations operated alongside cultural and youth groups. Population peaked around 2,000 by 1930, settling at 882 by 1940. Following Italian occupation from April 1941, remaining Jews were deported to Larissa and then death camps on March 24-25, 1944. Postwar recovery reached about 700 (including refugees from other communities), making Volos one of Greece's largest Jewish communities after Athens and Salonika. This cemetery's founding is unknown, presumed 19th century.
